paragraphs: The North of England is not one council area. It covers three English regions, the North East, the North West, and Yorkshire and the Humber, and children in care there are looked after by dozens of county, city and borough councils as well as by the independent agencies shown above, which take carers from across the north.

Several northern councils now recruit together. Foster with North East brings together twelve councils: Darlington, Durham, Gateshead, Hartlepool, Middlesbrough, Newcastle, Northumberland, North Tyneside, Redcar and Cleveland, South Tyneside, Stockton-on-Tees and Sunderland. It was the government's first pilot for regional recruitment, running since the end of 2023, and acts as the first stop for anyone thinking of fostering, passing them to their local council and supporting them through the application. After its first year, Sunderland reported more than 850 enquiries and an average of 4.8 months from application to approval. In the North West, Foster with Us does the same for Blackburn with Darwen, Blackpool, Lancashire, Cumberland, and Westmorland and Furness.

Every fostering service in the north must pay at least the national minimum allowance for the rest of England. For April 2026 to April 2027 that is £176 a week for a child aged 0 to 2, £182 for 3 to 4, £201 for 5 to 10, £227 for 11 to 15 and £267 for 16 to 17.

For local detail, start with the page for your own area: our North East England, North West England and Yorkshire pages, and town and county pages such as Newcastle, Sunderland, Greater Manchester and Lancashire. Then speak to your council and to two or three of the services above.
